_meta.purpose: Parameter bounds + priors for OECD-graph calibration

evidence_label_legend.literature_backed: central tendency taken from a peer-reviewed paper
evidence_label_legend.heuristic: no published prior; bounds set by engine validator
evidence_label_legend.engine_safeguard: not a scientific parameter; bounds set by stability checks

amplification_mu.citation: Carvalho, Nirei, Saito, Tahbaz-Salehi (2021) QJE — 3-4x indirect/direct multiplier on Tohoku → μ in [2, 3] consistent with that range
amplification_mu.notes: engine uses A_amp = amplification × (1 + μ × sigmoid((shock-threshold)/eps)). μ=2.5 puts max amplification at ~3.5x base

amplification_eps.notes: controls sigmoid sharpness; no published anchor

propagation_decay.notes: per-step decay of propagation impact; engine default 0.85

recovery_rate.citation: Cerra, Fatas, Saxena (2020) IMF WP — 1-2% permanent loss per recession implies slow recovery → ξ ≈ 0.02-0.10 weekly
recovery_rate.notes: per-week recovery rate when no external forcing

distress_base.notes: base threshold for distress accumulation; engine default 0.40

bullwhip_factor.citation: Lee, Padmanabhan, Whang (1997) Mgmt Science — Var(orders)/Var(demand) >= 1 + 2αL + 2α²L² bounded ~1-2 for typical sectors
bullwhip_factor.notes: applied to inbound when SEIRS E-state active

inventory_scale.citation: per-sector inventory weeks from seis.py INDUSTRY_INVENTORY_WEEKS (IHS Markit / SEMI / Boeing); inventory_scale is a global multiplier
inventory_scale.notes: scales per-node max_buffer; controls when E->I transition fires

r_output_floor.citation: Cerra et al. 2020 IMF WP — 1-2% permanent GDP loss implies hysteresis floor at low end of range; engine default 0.30 may be too high
r_output_floor.notes: minimum output_loss after R-state activation (hysteresis lower bound)

sanity_max_loss_fraction.notes: stability bound; not a scientific parameter but tuneable

metric_weights._meta: composite objective for MCMC: w_mae * MAE + w_rmse * RMSE + w_pearson * (1 - |Pearson|). Lower is better.

splits._note: Stratification: all non-scenario events sorted by event_id; first 16 to train, next 5 to val. Some event_ids may not appear in eligible if they fail OECD-graph remapping at runtime; in that case the actual split is the intersection.
